sourceFile: HOMOPHONES — Ultimate Cheat Codes (One Word per Page) - Word Pages.csv

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell accept
wordPages.cheatCode: ACCEPT begins with A for “Alright, I agree!” That's the one you say yes to.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two open arms shaped like a giant A catching a wrapped present.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell except
wordPages.cheatCode: EXCEPT starts with EX, as in EXclude: one thing is left OUT.
wordPages.imageDescription: A group of five cupcakes with one cupcake outside a giant EX-shaped circle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell affect
wordPages.cheatCode: AFFECT starts with A for ACTION: the wind acts on the tree.
wordPages.imageDescription: A large A-shaped gust bending one little tree sideways.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell effect
wordPages.cheatCode: EFFECT starts with E for END result: what happened after the action?
wordPages.imageDescription: A fallen tree beside a huge letter E-shaped arrow labelled as the outcome by its position.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell berry
wordPages.cheatCode: BERRY needs TWO Rs: picture two ripe raspberries side by side.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two bright red raspberries perched on twin letter-R stems.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bury
wordPages.cheatCode: BURY has U for UNDER: bury treasure UNDER the soil.
wordPages.imageDescription: A giant U-shaped hole with a treasure chest tucked at the bottom.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell breath
wordPages.cheatCode: One BREATH is one puff. It stops at TH—no extra E needed.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single round cloud of breath leaving a child's mouth, with a tiny TH on the cloud.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell breathe
wordPages.cheatCode: To BREATHE is to keep the air moving: add the extra E for EXHALE.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling pair of lungs blowing an E-shaped swirl of air.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell compliment
wordPages.cheatCode: A complIment is something kind I say. The letter I keeps the praise personal.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling letter I handing a heart-shaped compliment to a friend.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell complement
wordPages.cheatCode: ComplEment has E like complEte: two pieces make a perfect whole.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two E-shaped jigsaw pieces clicking together into one complete circle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell conscience
wordPages.cheatCode: CONSCIENCE contains SCIENCE: imagine a scientist checking right from wrong.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tiny scientist inside a heart examining a compass, with SCIENCE on the lab coat.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell conscious
wordPages.cheatCode: CONSCIOUS ends CIOUS, not CIENCE: eyes open, awake and aware.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two wide awake eyes peeking through two round O-shaped windows, with CIOUS beneath.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell descent
wordPages.cheatCode: DESCENT starts DESC, just like DESCEND: imagine going DOWN the steps.
wordPages.imageDescription: A steep staircase descending into a valley; the letters DESC form its handrail.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell dissent
wordPages.cheatCode: DISSENT starts DIS, like DISagree: stand up and say “No!”
wordPages.imageDescription: Two children voting; one holds a giant DIS-shaped thumbs-down sign.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell desert
wordPages.cheatCode: One S for the sandy DESERT. There isn't a second scoop in sight!
wordPages.imageDescription: One S-shaped sand dune with a tiny cactus and bright sun.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell dessert
wordPages.cheatCode: DeSSert has TWO Ss—one for each scoop of ice cream.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two scoops of ice cream shaped like the letters S and S in a bowl.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell draft
wordPages.cheatCode: A DRAFT is a quick first drawing. Its spelling is quick too—no AUGHT.
wordPages.imageDescription: A rough pencil sketch on a sheet, with the word's last FT shaped like two pencils.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell draught
wordPages.cheatCode: DRAUGHT has AUGHT like CAUGHT: a cold draught CAUGHT me shivering!
wordPages.imageDescription: A surprised child caught by a chilly ribbon of wind beneath a door; AUGHT swirls in the breeze.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell especially
wordPages.cheatCode: ESPECIALLY begins with an EXTRA E: something is especially important.
wordPages.imageDescription: A gold star wearing an oversized glittery E at its very front.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell specially
wordPages.cheatCode: SPECIALLY starts straight with SPECIAL: made for a special purpose.
wordPages.imageDescription: One specially wrapped present with a giant S-shaped ribbon and no initial E.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell farther
wordPages.cheatCode: FAR is right at the start of FARTHER—think of a faraway finish line.
wordPages.imageDescription: A road stretching FAR into the distance with a giant R at the horizon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell father
wordPages.cheatCode: FATHER starts FA like FAMILY. FARTHER has an extra R for FAR away.
wordPages.imageDescription: A family portrait with a dad and child standing inside a big FA-shaped photo frame.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell led
wordPages.cheatCode: Yesterday you LED the way. The A from LEAD has already left.
wordPages.imageDescription: A leader reaching yesterday's finish line while an A-shaped balloon floats away.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell lead
wordPages.cheatCode: LEAD keeps its A, just like LEADER: today I lead the team.
wordPages.imageDescription: A team captain wearing a large golden A badge at the front of a group.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell loose
wordPages.cheatCode: LOOSE has TWO Os, like two loops in a belt that's too loose.
wordPages.imageDescription: A loose belt with two enormous O-shaped holes hanging open.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell lose
wordPages.cheatCode: LOSE has LOST an O! Only one O remains.
wordPages.imageDescription: A worried child chasing a giant runaway letter O.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell of
wordPages.cheatCode: OF has just one F: a piece OF cake connects cake and piece.
wordPages.imageDescription: One giant F-shaped fork connecting a cake to its slice.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell off
wordPages.cheatCode: OFF has TWO Fs, like two fingers flicking a switch OFF.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two F-shaped fingers pushing a light switch down.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell precede
wordPages.cheatCode: PRECEDE starts PRE, like PREvious: it comes BEFORE something else.
wordPages.imageDescription: A huge PRE-shaped arrow arriving first at a starting line.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell proceed
wordPages.cheatCode: PROCEED starts PRO, like PROgress: keep going FORWARD.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cheerful green PRO-shaped arrow marching down a path.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell principal
wordPages.cheatCode: Your school PRINCIPAL ends in PAL—imagine the headteacher as your PAL.
wordPages.imageDescription: A friendly headteacher high-fiving a giant smiling PAL-shaped mascot.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell principle
wordPages.cheatCode: A PRINCIPLE is a ruLE you follow. Both finish in LE.
wordPages.imageDescription: A classroom rule poster with two huge letter tiles L and E at its base.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell quite
wordPages.cheatCode: QUITE puts the E at the END: you're quite finished!
wordPages.imageDescription: An E triumphantly crossing a finish line after a T, like the last runner.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell quiet
wordPages.cheatCode: QUIET slips its E in BEFORE the T—tiptoe without a sound.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tiny letter E tiptoeing past a tall T in a hushed library.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell advice
wordPages.cheatCode: ADVICE ends ICE: a “piece of advice” is a thing you can receive.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tiny block of ice shaped like the letters ICE holding a helpful note.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell advise
wordPages.cheatCode: ADVISE ends ISE: I adviSe you by SAYING what might help.
wordPages.imageDescription: A teacher speaking through a giant letter S-shaped megaphone.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell device
wordPages.cheatCode: DEVICE ends ICE: a device is a THING you can hold.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tiny robot gadget sitting inside an ICE-shaped transparent ice block.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell devise
wordPages.cheatCode: DEVISE ends ISE: you use your IDEAS to devise a plan.
wordPages.imageDescription: A child drawing a brilliant plan with a pencil tracing a giant letter S.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell licence
wordPages.cheatCode: In British English, LICENCE has C for CARD: a licence is the document you carry.
wordPages.imageDescription: A driving licence card held in front of a giant C-shaped holder.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell license
wordPages.cheatCode: In British English, LICENSE has S for STAMP: to license is to grant permission.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling official using a huge S-shaped rubber stamp to approve a permit.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell practice
wordPages.cheatCode: In British English, PRACTICE with C is a THING: your tennis practice.
wordPages.imageDescription: A calendar with a big C-shaped tennis court marked as a practice session.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell practise
wordPages.cheatCode: In British English, PRACTISE with S is something you DO: swing, spell, sing!
wordPages.imageDescription: A child practising tennis with a racket leaving a huge S-shaped swing trail.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell prophecy
wordPages.cheatCode: A PROPHECY is a prediction you can hear or read: C for CRYSTAL BALL.
wordPages.imageDescription: A crystal ball with a large glowing letter C inside, showing tomorrow's weather.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell prophesy
wordPages.cheatCode: To PROPHESY is to SAY what will happen: S for SPEAK.
wordPages.imageDescription: A storyteller speaking into an S-shaped microphone with a tiny future scene above it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell wary
wordPages.cheatCode: WARY begins WAR: a castle guard must be wary and watch for danger.
wordPages.imageDescription: An alert, friendly castle guard peering out from behind a big WAR-shaped wall.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell weary
wordPages.cheatCode: WEARY hides EAR: when you're weary, even your ears look sleepy.
wordPages.imageDescription: A sleepy bunny with two long, drooping E-A-R-shaped ears.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell aisle
wordPages.cheatCode: AISLE starts AI like AIRPLANE: walk down the airplane aisle.
wordPages.imageDescription: The empty central aisle of an aeroplane, with A and I shaped seat dividers.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell isle
wordPages.cheatCode: ISLE starts IS like ISLAND: a little island in the sea.
wordPages.imageDescription: A small green island shaped like the letters I and S, surrounded by blue water.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell allowed
wordPages.cheatCode: ALLOWED keeps ALLOW: being allowed means someone says you may.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling gatekeeper opening a gate with a green ALLOW-shaped key.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell aloud
wordPages.cheatCode: ALOUD has LOUD inside it: if you read aloud, let the words be heard.
wordPages.imageDescription: A megaphone blasting a big, rounded LOUD-shaped sound wave.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell altar
wordPages.cheatCode: ALTAR ends AR: think A Religious table in a church.
wordPages.imageDescription: One simple altar table holding two candles bent into the shapes A and R.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell alter
wordPages.cheatCode: ALTER ends ER for EDIT and REPLACE: alter means change something.
wordPages.imageDescription: An artist changing a plain shirt with an E-shaped eraser and an R-shaped paintbrush.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell ascent
wordPages.cheatCode: ASCENT has SC for STAIR CLIMB: going up, up, up!
wordPages.imageDescription: A tall staircase winding uphill, with S and C shaped steps near the top.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell assent
wordPages.cheatCode: ASSENT has SS for SAY SO: to assent is to agree.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two friendly letter-S characters nodding yes and giving thumbs-up.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell ball
wordPages.cheatCode: BALL ends ALL: we can ALL play with a ball.
wordPages.imageDescription: A colourful football with three big letter-shaped patches A-L-L.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bawl
wordPages.cheatCode: BAWL has AW: imagine someone crying “AW!” really loudly.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cartoon baby crying two gigantic teardrops shaped A and W.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bare
wordPages.cheatCode: BARE contains ARE: ARE your feet wearing shoes? No—bare feet!
wordPages.imageDescription: Two bare feet next to an empty pair of shoes and a giant question mark.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bear
wordPages.cheatCode: BEAR hides EAR: every bear has ears.
wordPages.imageDescription: A fluffy teddy bear whose ears are giant letters E-A-R.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell be
wordPages.cheatCode: BE means exist—it's the short word, with just one E.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single letter B standing beside exactly one little E like two friends.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bee
wordPages.cheatCode: BEE buzzes for longer: add an extra E to make BEEE!
wordPages.imageDescription: One bee flying and pulling a second bright letter E behind its first E.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell blue
wordPages.cheatCode: BLUE has U for UP: look UP at the blue sky.
wordPages.imageDescription: A huge blue letter U floating in an otherwise clear blue sky.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell blew
wordPages.cheatCode: BLEW has EW like flEW: the wind blew and a leaf flew!
wordPages.imageDescription: A windy swirl carrying a leaf with letters E and W blowing behind it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell brake
wordPages.cheatCode: BRAKE has A, as in cAr: press the brake to stop the car.
wordPages.imageDescription: A bright red A-shaped brake pedal beneath a car dashboard.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell break
wordPages.cheatCode: BREAK has EA like tEAr: tear a biscuit in two and it breaks.
wordPages.imageDescription: A biscuit cracking in two, with E and A on the broken halves.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bridal
wordPages.cheatCode: BRIDAL has A for the wedding DAY: a bridal dress is for the bride.
wordPages.imageDescription: A wedding dress on a hanger with a big letter A sewn into its ribbon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bridle
wordPages.cheatCode: BRIDLE has E for horsE: it's the straps on a horse's head.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling horse wearing a bridle, with a prominent E-shaped buckle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell cereal
wordPages.cheatCode: CEREAL starts C for CORNFLAKES: breakfast in a bowl.
wordPages.imageDescription: One bowl of cereal with a huge C-shaped cornflake on top.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell serial
wordPages.cheatCode: SERIAL starts S for SERIES: events or episodes happen one after another.
wordPages.imageDescription: A row of three storybook episodes connected by one long S-shaped ribbon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell guessed
wordPages.cheatCode: GUESSED = GUESS + ED: yesterday you made your guess.
wordPages.imageDescription: A detective holding a guessed answer card with bright E-and-D tiles added.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell guest
wordPages.cheatCode: GUEST ends ST: a SPECIAL TRAVELLER comes to visit.
wordPages.imageDescription: A welcomed traveller carrying an S-shaped suitcase and T-shaped hat.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell least
wordPages.cheatCode: LEAST ends ST like smalleST: the least is the smallest amount.
wordPages.imageDescription: Three heaps of sweets; the tiniest sits on an S-and-T-shaped tray.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell leased
wordPages.cheatCode: LEASED = LEASE + D: the shop was leased to a new tenant.
wordPages.imageDescription: A shop key resting on a lease agreement with one large D-shaped paperclip.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell missed
wordPages.cheatCode: MISSED = MISS + ED: “I missed the bus” happened yesterday.
wordPages.imageDescription: A bus driving away while a child waves, with two trailing letter tiles E and D.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell mist
wordPages.cheatCode: MIST ends ST, like FROST: both can make a chilly morning look hazy.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single misty cloud swirling around an S-and-T-shaped frosty branch.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell packed
wordPages.cheatCode: PACKED = PACK + ED: the suitcase was packed yesterday.
wordPages.imageDescription: A closed, packed suitcase with bright letter tiles E and D clipped to the handle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell pact
wordPages.cheatCode: PACT contains ACT: in a pact, you agree to ACT together.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two children sealing a pinky promise beneath one giant A-C-T-shaped arch.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell past
wordPages.cheatCode: PAST ends AST like LAST: last week is in the past.
wordPages.imageDescription: A calendar showing LAST week, with a huge torn-off page marked by a giant T.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell passed
wordPages.cheatCode: PASSED = PASS + ED: the ball was passed yesterday.
wordPages.imageDescription: A ball flying from one player to another along an E-and-D-shaped path.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell fair
wordPages.cheatCode: FAIR hides AIR: the fairground rides whizz through the air.
wordPages.imageDescription: A fairground chair swing soaring in AIR with AIR-shaped ribbons.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell fare
wordPages.cheatCode: FARE is the price of a journey: think FAREWELL as you buy a ticket.
wordPages.imageDescription: One train ticket beside a waving hand saying goodbye, with a big FARE stamp.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell grate
wordPages.cheatCode: GRATE has GRATER inside its family: you grate cheese with a grater.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cheese grater making a pile of yellow cheese curls shaped like the letter A.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell great
wordPages.cheatCode: GREAT contains EAT: a GREAT cake is something GREAT to EAT.
wordPages.imageDescription: A giant delicious cake with the letters E-A-T made of icing.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell groan
wordPages.cheatCode: GROAN ends OAN, like MOAN: “Oh no!”
wordPages.imageDescription: One disgruntled character groaning into a speech bubble shaped O-A-N.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell grown
wordPages.cheatCode: GROWN starts GROW: a seed has grown into a tall plant.
wordPages.imageDescription: One sprout growing into a giant sunflower with GROW rising up the stalk.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell heel
wordPages.cheatCode: HEEL has TWO Es: picture TWO heels at the back of your shoes.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two heels of shoes turned into the two letters E and E.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell he'll
wordPages.cheatCode: HE'LL means HE WILL: the apostrophe hides the missing WI.
wordPages.imageDescription: A big apostrophe acting as a curtain hiding WI between HE and LL.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell heal
wordPages.cheatCode: HEAL begins HEALTHY: to heal is to become healthy again.
wordPages.imageDescription: A small bandage patch shaped like A on a knee, beside a giant cheerful heart.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell here
wordPages.cheatCode: HERE has TWO Es: put two feet down and stand HERE.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two little E-shaped boots planted on one spot on a map.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell hear
wordPages.cheatCode: HEAR hides EAR: ears are made for hearing!
wordPages.imageDescription: One giant friendly ear built around the letters EAR.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell knot
wordPages.cheatCode: KNOT starts KN like KNIT: tie a knot in the wool.
wordPages.imageDescription: A length of knitting wool tied into an enormous letter K-shaped knot.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell not
wordPages.cheatCode: NOT begins NO: no, that is NOT right!
wordPages.imageDescription: A huge NO-shaped red cross on a wrong answer.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell mail
wordPages.cheatCode: MAIL contains AIRMAIL: imagine a letter flying through the air.
wordPages.imageDescription: One envelope with a wing made from the letters A and I.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell male
wordPages.cheatCode: MALE is hiding inside FEMALE: take away FE and the word MALE remains.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two magnetic letter tiles F and E floating away from FEMALE to leave MALE.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell main
wordPages.cheatCode: MAIN finishes AIN, like BRAIN: your BRAIN finds the MAIN idea.
wordPages.imageDescription: A happy cartoon brain lifting the number-one main idea, with AIN glowing.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell mane
wordPages.cheatCode: MANE ends E, like horsE: picture a horse's long mane.
wordPages.imageDescription: A horse with a flowing mane that ends in a giant curly E-shaped lock.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell meat
wordPages.cheatCode: MEAT contains EAT: meat is something people EAT.
wordPages.imageDescription: A dinner plate with the three letters E-A-T shaped like food pieces.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell meet
wordPages.cheatCode: MEET has TWO Es: TWO people come face to face.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two friends shaking hands while standing inside twin E-shaped doorways.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell medal
wordPages.cheatCode: MEDAL has A for AWARD: you win a medal for your achievement.
wordPages.imageDescription: A bright gold medal hanging from a giant letter A-shaped ribbon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell meddle
wordPages.cheatCode: MEDDLE has DD for DON'T DIG into other people's business.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two giant D-shaped shovels nosily digging into someone else's sandcastle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell morning
wordPages.cheatCode: MORNING begins MORN: another word for dawn. No extra U.
wordPages.imageDescription: A glowing sunrise peeking above a giant M-shaped hill.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell mourning
wordPages.cheatCode: MOURNING has U: turn a U upside down to make a sad little frown.
wordPages.imageDescription: A gentle sad face whose mouth is a large upside-down U, with a small flower beside it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell night
wordPages.cheatCode: NIGHT begins N for NAP: stars come out when it's time to sleep.
wordPages.imageDescription: A sleepy moon snuggled inside a big N-shaped nightcap.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell knight
wordPages.cheatCode: KNIGHT begins K for KING: a knight guards a king.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cartoon knight wearing a large K-shaped shield beside a castle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell one
wordPages.cheatCode: ONE has ONE O: one balloon, one candle, one of a kind.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single O-shaped balloon floating above one candle.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell won
wordPages.cheatCode: WON starts W like WIN: yesterday you WON the race.
wordPages.imageDescription: A gold winner's trophy with a huge W as its handles.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell plain
wordPages.cheatCode: PLAIN has AIN like RAIN: picture a plain grey raincoat with no pattern.
wordPages.imageDescription: A completely plain grey raincoat, with one raindrop shaped like the letters AI.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell plane
wordPages.cheatCode: PLANE hides LANE: an aeroplane races down a long runway lane.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cartoon aeroplane on a runway with the letters LANE forming the runway.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell profit
wordPages.cheatCode: PROFIT contains FIT: money left after costs can FIT in a piggy bank.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling piggy bank with the coins arranging themselves into the word FIT.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell prophet
wordPages.cheatCode: PROPHET has PH like PHONE: imagine a prophet phoning with a prediction.
wordPages.imageDescription: A friendly storybook fortune-teller speaking into a big PH-shaped telephone.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell rain
wordPages.cheatCode: RAIN finishes AIN, like DRAIN: rain runs down the drain.
wordPages.imageDescription: A big raindrop sliding down into a drain shaped like the letters A-I-N.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell rein
wordPages.cheatCode: REIN starts REIN, as in REINDEER: Santa holds the reins of his reindeer.
wordPages.imageDescription: Santa's gloved hand holding one leather rein attached to a reindeer.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell reign
wordPages.cheatCode: REIGN has G for GOVERN: a king or queen governs during a reign.
wordPages.imageDescription: A gold crown resting on a huge glittery G-shaped throne.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell scene
wordPages.cheatCode: SCENE starts SC for STAGE CURTAIN: a scene happens on a stage.
wordPages.imageDescription: A red stage curtain opening to reveal one giant S-and-C-shaped spotlight.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell seen
wordPages.cheatCode: SEEN has two Es like two EYES: “I've seen it!”
wordPages.imageDescription: Two large E-shaped eyes watching a bright shooting star.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell sent
wordPages.cheatCode: SENT starts S like SEND: I sent the letter after I wrote it.
wordPages.imageDescription: An envelope whooshing into a postbox along an S-shaped flight path.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell cent
wordPages.cheatCode: CENT starts C like COIN: one cent is a coin.
wordPages.imageDescription: A huge shiny one-cent coin with a bold C punched into it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell scent
wordPages.cheatCode: SCENT begins SC for SMELLY CANDLE: follow the smell!
wordPages.imageDescription: A scented candle sending up two curls of smoke shaped S and C.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell stationary
wordPages.cheatCode: STATIONARY has A for stAnd still: nothing moves.
wordPages.imageDescription: A bright toy train stopped dead at a station, with a huge A-shaped stop barrier.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell stationery
wordPages.cheatCode: STATIONERY has E for ENVELOPE: pens, paper and letters.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single enormous E-shaped envelope with a colourful pencil tucked inside.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell steal
wordPages.cheatCode: STEAL has A for AWAY: steal means take something away without permission.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cartoon magpie carrying a stolen shiny key away in its A-shaped beak.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell steel
wordPages.cheatCode: STEEL has TWO Es, like two sturdy metal beams.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two tall shiny steel beams bent into matching letter Es.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell sun
wordPages.cheatCode: SUN has U for UP: the sun is UP in the sky.
wordPages.imageDescription: A smiling sun rising inside a giant U-shaped golden horizon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell son
wordPages.cheatCode: SON has O like bOy: someone's son is their boy.
wordPages.imageDescription: A happy boy holding a large O-shaped family photo frame.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell whether
wordPages.cheatCode: WHETHER begins WH like WHICH: “Which one? Whether to go or stay?”
wordPages.imageDescription: A fork in a road with a giant W-and-H-shaped question mark above it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell weather
wordPages.cheatCode: WEATHER has EA like hEAt: think sunshine, rain and snow outside.
wordPages.imageDescription: A sunny cloud wearing an E-and-A-shaped pair of sunglasses.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell he'll
wordPages.cheatCode: HE'LL means HE WILL: the apostrophe hides the missing WI.
wordPages.imageDescription: A big apostrophe acting as a curtain hiding WI between HE and LL.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell hell
wordPages.cheatCode: HELL has no apostrophe: in stories, it's a fiery underworld, not “he will”.
wordPages.imageDescription: A harmless storybook lava cave shaped like two letter L pillars, with no apostrophe.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell I'll
wordPages.cheatCode: I'LL = I WILL: hide WI behind an apostrophe.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tall letter I standing next to an apostrophe curtain concealing W and I.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell ill
wordPages.cheatCode: ILL means unwell: no apostrophe when you're feeling ill.
wordPages.imageDescription: A child resting in bed beside three cosy letter-shaped pillows I-L-L.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell it's
wordPages.cheatCode: IT'S = IT IS or IT HAS: the apostrophe holds the missing letters.
wordPages.imageDescription: A tiny apostrophe bridging two puzzle pieces marked IT and IS.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell its
wordPages.cheatCode: ITS means belonging to IT, just like HIS means belonging to HIM—no apostrophe.
wordPages.imageDescription: A cat proudly holding its own tail like a soft S-shaped ribbon.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell let's
wordPages.cheatCode: LET'S = LET US: the apostrophe takes the place of U.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two friends opening a gate; a giant apostrophe floats where the U disappeared.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell lets
wordPages.cheatCode: LETS = LET + S: someone LETS you do something. No apostrophe.
wordPages.imageDescription: A friendly parent opening a gate with a large S-shaped key.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell she'd
wordPages.cheatCode: SHE'D = SHE HAD or SHE WOULD: the apostrophe hides letters.
wordPages.imageDescription: A girl lifting an apostrophe-shaped curtain to reveal HAD and WOULD behind it.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell shed
wordPages.cheatCode: SHED is a garden building, not SHE'D. No apostrophe in the roof.
wordPages.imageDescription: One neat garden shed with a roof built from two giant E-shaped tiles.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell she'll
wordPages.cheatCode: SHE'LL = SHE WILL: the apostrophe replaces WI.
wordPages.imageDescription: One girl pointing to the future, a glowing apostrophe hiding WI beside her.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell shell
wordPages.cheatCode: SHELL has no apostrophe: a seashell has two L-shaped ridges.
wordPages.imageDescription: A single pearly seashell with two distinct L-shaped grooves.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell we'd
wordPages.cheatCode: WE'D = WE HAD or WE WOULD: the apostrophe hides letters.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two friends holding a giant comma-shaped apostrophe umbrella over a missing word.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell wed
wordPages.cheatCode: WED begins WED like WEDDING: the couple wed, no apostrophe.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two cartoon wedding rings linked in the shape of W, E and D.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell we'll
wordPages.cheatCode: WE'LL = WE WILL: the apostrophe replaces WI.
wordPages.imageDescription: Three friends about to act, with WI disappearing under an oversized apostrophe.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell well
wordPages.cheatCode: WELL has no apostrophe: picture a water well with two tall L-shaped posts.
wordPages.imageDescription: A round stone water well with two clear tall L-shaped wooden supports.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell we're
wordPages.cheatCode: WE'RE = WE ARE: the apostrophe replaces the A.
wordPages.imageDescription: A little A popping out of WE ARE and leaving an apostrophe-shaped gap.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell were
wordPages.cheatCode: WERE starts WE: “WE WERE there yesterday.”
wordPages.imageDescription: Two children looking back at a calendar marked yesterday, with a huge WE in front.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell by
wordPages.cheatCode: BY is tiny: two letters sitting right BY each other.
wordPages.imageDescription: Two letters B and Y sitting side-by-side on a little park bench.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell bye
wordPages.cheatCode: BYE ends E like wavE: wave goodbye and say BYE.
wordPages.imageDescription: One waving hand leaving a giant E-shaped motion trail.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell buy
wordPages.cheatCode: BUY has U for YOU: YOU pay money when you BUY.
wordPages.imageDescription: A shopper shaped like a big U dropping a coin into a till.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell for
wordPages.cheatCode: FOR has NO U: a present is FOR you, not the number FOUR.
wordPages.imageDescription: A present with a small gift tag reading FOR and an extra U floating away.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell four
wordPages.cheatCode: FOUR has U: picture FOUR fingers and one thumb tucked away.
wordPages.imageDescription: A hand holding up four fingers, with a huge U circling those four fingers.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell our
wordPages.cheatCode: OUR is hiding in YOUR. Take away the Y when something belongs to US.
wordPages.imageDescription: A large Y lifting away from the front of a shared team flag, leaving O-U-R.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell hour
wordPages.cheatCode: HOUR has H for HANDS: clock hands show the hour.
wordPages.imageDescription: One big clock with the hands forming a very clear letter H.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell who's
wordPages.cheatCode: WHO'S = WHO IS or WHO HAS: the apostrophe hides the missing letters.
wordPages.imageDescription: A detective holding an enormous apostrophe-shaped magnifying glass over WHO IS.

wordPages.pageHeading: The ultimate cheat code to remember how to spell whose
wordPages.cheatCode: WHOSE hides HOSE: WHOSE garden HOSE is this?
wordPages.imageDescription: A long green garden hose twisted into the letters H-O-S-E.
